en: Yesterday I missed the bus, so I walked to the office.
tamil: நேத்து பஸ்ஸை விட்டுட்டேன், அதனால ஆபீஸ் வரைக்கும் நடந்தே போனேன்.
context: Explaining to a colleague why you looked tired.
explain: 'Missed' and 'walked' are past tense. 'So' joins a result to its reason.
usage: Use it with colleagues to explain a small problem from the day before.
leelaQ: What happened to you on the way to work yesterday?
answer: Yesterday I missed the bus, so I took an auto.

en: What happened to you yesterday?
tamil: நேத்து உனக்கு என்ன ஆச்சு?
context: Asking a colleague why they were absent.
explain: 'What happened?' asks about an event. Use it to show concern.
usage: Use it with a colleague or friend who missed something.
leelaQ: Why did you miss the office or class last time?
answer: I missed it because I had a fever.

en: We went to Ooty last summer and it rained every day.
tamil: போன கோடையில ஊட்டிக்கு போனோம், தினமும் மழை பெய்துச்சு.
context: Telling a friend about a holiday.
explain: 'Went' is the past of 'go'. 'Last summer' tells when it happened.
usage: Use it when you share a trip story with friends or relatives.
leelaQ: Where did you go for your last holiday?
answer: We went to Munnar last year and the weather was lovely.

en: Please tell me what happened at the bank.
tamil: பேங்க்ல என்ன நடந்துச்சுன்னு தயவு செய்து சொல்லுங்க.
context: Asking a family member for the full story.
explain: 'Please tell me' is a polite request. 'What happened' follows without a question form.
usage: Use it with family or friends when you want the whole story.
leelaQ: Can you tell me about a time you went to a bank?
answer: I went to open an account and waited for an hour.

en: When I was small, I used to catch fish in the village pond.
tamil: நான் சின்னவனா இருந்தப்போ ஊர் குளத்துல மீன் பிடிப்பேன்.
context: Sharing a childhood memory with friends.
explain: 'Used to' talks about a habit in the past that does not happen now.
usage: Use it to talk about childhood with friends, cousins or new colleagues.
leelaQ: What did you love doing when you were a child?
answer: I used to play cricket in the street every evening.

en: I did not sleep well last night because of the noise.
tamil: சத்தம் காரணமா நேத்து ராத்திரி நல்லா தூங்கல.
context: Telling a colleague why you look tired.
explain: Negative past: 'did not' plus the base verb 'sleep'.
usage: Use it to explain tiredness to a friend or manager.
leelaQ: How did you sleep last night?
answer: I slept well because the night was cool.

en: I have visited Madurai three times this year.
tamil: இந்த வருஷம் மூணு தடவை மதுரைக்கு போயிருக்கேன்.
context: Telling a friend how often you travelled.
explain: Present perfect (have + visited) links past visits with now. 'This year' is not finished yet.
usage: Use it to say how many times you did something up to now.
leelaQ: How many times have you travelled this year?
answer: I have travelled four times this year, mostly for work.

en: Where did you go last weekend?
tamil: போன வார இறுதியில எங்க போனீங்க?
context: Starting a Monday chat with a friend.
explain: Use 'did' plus the base verb 'go' in past questions. Do not say 'did you went'.
usage: Use it on Monday to start a friendly talk at work or college.
leelaQ: What did you do on the last weekend?
answer: I went to my native place with my family.

en: First I called the mechanic, then I waited near the bike for an hour.
tamil: முதல்ல மெக்கானிக்கை கூப்பிட்டேன், அப்புறம் வண்டி பக்கத்துலயே ஒரு மணி நேரம் காத்திருந்தேன்.
context: Describing what happened when your bike broke down.
explain: 'First' and 'then' show the order of events in a story.
usage: Use it to tell events in order when you explain a problem to a friend.
leelaQ: What did you do when your vehicle broke down?
answer: First I stopped on the side, then I called my brother.

en: Did you enjoy the trip to Kodaikanal?
tamil: கொடைக்கானல் டிரிப் ரசிச்சீங்களா?
context: Asking a friend after their holiday.
explain: Past yes/no questions start with 'Did' and use the base verb.
usage: Use it when a friend or colleague comes back from a trip.
leelaQ: Did you enjoy your last trip, and why?
answer: Yes, I enjoyed it because the weather was cool.

en: My phone fell into the water, and I panicked.
tamil: என் ஃபோன் தண்ணில விழுந்துடுச்சு, நான் பயந்துட்டேன்.
context: Telling a friend about a small accident.
explain: 'Fell' is the irregular past of 'fall'. 'Panicked' shows a sudden fear.
usage: Use it to share a stressful moment in a casual chat.
leelaQ: Have you ever dropped your phone? What happened?
answer: Yes, I dropped it in the bucket and it stopped working.

en: Could you tell me how the interview went?
tamil: இன்டர்வியூ எப்படி போச்சுன்னு சொல்ல முடியுமா?
context: Asking a friend after a job interview.
explain: 'Could you' is polite. 'How the interview went' stays in statement order.
usage: Use it to politely ask about someone's recent experience.
leelaQ: How did your last interview or exam go?
answer: It went well, and I answered most questions.

en: After we finished lunch, we all went to see a movie.
tamil: சாப்பிட்டு முடிச்சப்புறம் எல்லாரும் சினிமாவுக்கு போனோம்.
context: Telling a colleague about a family outing.
explain: 'After' joins two past events. The first event happened before the second.
usage: Use it to tell what you did after a meal or event.
leelaQ: What did you do last Sunday after lunch?
answer: After lunch we rested for some time and then visited my aunt.

en: We have not met each other since college.
tamil: காலேஜுக்கு அப்புறம் நாங்க ஒருத்தரை ஒருத்தர் பார்க்கவே இல்ல.
context: Talking about an old friend.
explain: 'Have not' with 'since' shows a long time without an action.
usage: Use it when you talk about an old friend you have lost touch with.
leelaQ: Who is an old friend you haven't met for years?
answer: I have not met my school friend Ravi for ten years.

en: I have just come back from my cousin's wedding.
tamil: நான் இப்பதான் என் மாமா பையன் கல்யாணத்துல இருந்து வந்தேன்.
context: Telling a neighbour where you were.
explain: 'Have just' means something finished a very short time ago.
usage: Use it when someone asks where you were, or why you are tired.
leelaQ: Have you been to a wedding recently?
answer: Yes, I have just attended my friend's wedding in Salem.

en: Have you ever been to Rameswaram?
tamil: நீங்க எப்பவாவது ராமேஸ்வரம் போயிருக்கீங்களா?
context: Asking about someone's travel experience.
explain: 'Have you ever...?' asks about experience in a whole life.
usage: Use it to ask new friends about places they have visited.
leelaQ: Have you ever been to a famous temple town?
answer: Yes, I have been to Madurai and Tirupati.

en: Last month my brother lost his wallet in the train.
tamil: போன மாசம் என் தம்பி ரயில்ல பர்ஸை தொலைச்சுட்டான்.
context: Telling a friend about a family problem.
explain: 'Lost' is the past of 'lose'. 'Last month' tells us when.
usage: Use it to tell a friend a sad or unlucky event from the past.
leelaQ: Did you ever lose something important?
answer: Yes, I once lost my ID card in the market.

en: What did you do after the exam finished?
tamil: பரீட்சை முடிஞ்சப்புறம் என்ன பண்ணுனீங்க?
context: Asking a friend about the day of the exam.
explain: 'What did you do' asks about an action. 'After' adds the time order.
usage: Use it to ask what someone did after an event.
leelaQ: What did you do after your last exam?
answer: I went home and slept for a few hours.

en: I was cooking when the gas cylinder ran out.
tamil: நான் சமைச்சுட்டு இருந்தப்போ கேஸ் சிலிண்டர் தீர்ந்துடுச்சு.
context: Telling a neighbour about a kitchen problem.
explain: Past continuous (was cooking) shows the long action. Simple past (ran out) shows the sudden one.
usage: Use it to explain what you were doing when something suddenly happened.
leelaQ: What were you doing when the power went off?
answer: I was watching TV when the power went off.

en: Tell me about your last holiday.
tamil: உங்க கடைசி விடுமுறையை பத்தி சொல்லுங்க.
context: Chatting with a new friend.
explain: A simple imperative to invite someone to tell their story.
usage: Use it in casual chats to start a story.
leelaQ: Where did you spend your last holiday?
answer: I went to Pondicherry and enjoyed the beach.

en: Finally, the auto driver found the right street after one hour.
tamil: கடைசியா ஆட்டோ டிரைவர் ஒரு மணி நேரம் கழிச்சு சரியான தெருவை கண்டுபிடிச்சார்.
context: Telling a friend about a long journey.
explain: 'Finally' shows the last event in a story after some waiting.
usage: Use it at the end of a story to show the problem was solved.
leelaQ: Have you ever got lost in a new place?
answer: Yes, I got lost in Bangalore and a shopkeeper showed me the way.

en: He never told me about the accident.
tamil: அவன் விபத்தை பத்தி எனக்கு எப்பவுமே சொல்லல.
context: Complaining that a friend hid something.
explain: 'Never' makes the sentence negative. It is used with a past verb.
usage: Use it when someone did not share important news with you.
leelaQ: Do you like to share bad news with friends?
answer: Yes, I share it so they can help me.

en: We have lived in this house for ten years.
tamil: நாங்க இந்த வீட்டுல பத்து வருஷமா இருக்கோம்.
context: Telling a new neighbour about yourself.
explain: Present perfect with 'for' shows something that started in the past and still continues.
usage: Use it when you talk about how long you have stayed in a place.
leelaQ: How long have you lived in your present house?
answer: We have lived here for five years.

en: Who told you about the accident?
tamil: அந்த விபத்தை பத்தி உங்களுக்கு யாரு சொன்னாங்க?
context: Asking a family member how they heard bad news.
explain: 'Who' asks about the person. After 'who' in a past question, use the past verb directly.
usage: Use it to find out the source of news in a serious situation.
leelaQ: How do you usually get the news every day?
answer: I read it on my phone in the morning.

en: My grandmother used to tell us stories every night.
tamil: எங்க பாட்டி தினமும் ராத்திரி எங்களுக்கு கதை சொல்லுவாங்க.
context: Remembering your childhood with a friend.
explain: 'Used to' shows a regular habit in the past.
usage: Use it to share warm family memories in a chat.
leelaQ: Who told you stories when you were small?
answer: My grandfather told me stories before I slept.
